Good morning Tara / Chris —

Thanks again for the sync last week. Per our MAP, this is the weekly checkpoint to align on the remaining close timeline and to lock the runbook owners ahead of the May 20th launch window. Key items for this week:

- Runbook v3 attached (runbook_v3.docx) — suggested owners highlighted in comments.
- Evaluation matrix: we still need final pass on the acceptance metrics and thresholds (latency P95, token-cost cap, and edge-case regression test pass rate).
- Cutover & fallback: Monica has a proposed rollback sequence that avoids DB migration during peak windows; see section 4 of the runbook.

Asks for CardioSense team: please confirm the primary approver for the acceptance gate and confirm the on-call contact for the first 48 hours after cutover.

I propose a 30m checkpoint today at 4:00pm PT to walk the runbook and action roster. If that works, I'll send a calendar hold.

All —

Per our discussion in today's checkpoint (thanks everyone for joining), I recorded the cutover rundown and sketched a compact rollback/stoplight. Summary of the most critical runbook points (see cutover_checklist.pdf attached for full checklist):

1) Pre-cutover (T-72 to T-1): smoke-eval runs nightly; freeze on non-essential infra changes at T-24. Owners: Monica (runbook), Ben (load infra), Tara/CardioSense (prompt-set finalization).
2) Cutover window (May 20, 00:00–03:00 PT): staged traffic shift 10% increments every 30 minutes with health checks at each stage. If token-cost spike > 20% or latency P95 > 400ms for two consecutive intervals, trigger rollback.
3) Rollback sequence: remove traffic split, revert model variant to previous stable tag, toggle caching profile to conservative, and re-open feature gate. Estimated recovery time: 18–45 minutes depending on cache warm-up.
4) Communications: runbook has pre-written status messages for customers and internal slack escalation templates.

Action owners (finalized):
- Runbook owner & cutover lead: Monica Patel — primary contact during window.
- Load testing & infra: Ben Carter — verify Dedicated capacity and burst thresholds.
- Acceptance metrics & monitoring: Karthik Iyer — dashboards and alerts.
- CardioSense acceptance approver: Lena Ortiz (VP Product) — to sign off on acceptance criteria pre-cutover.

Next steps: Monica will post the finalized cutover_checklist.pdf and runbook comments by EOD 05-04. CardioSense to deliver prompt-set by 05-06 so Monica can finalize smoke-eval config.

Monica Patel
Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
